rounds.proof_sketch: The mutation is on line 64 in `tanh_activation_kernel_half`, which is only called when `std::is_same<scalar_t, at::Half>::value` is true. The input specification mandates `dtype=torch.float32`, which dispatches to `tanh_activation_kernel_vectorized<float>` instead. The half-precision kernel path is never executed.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutant survives because the mutation affects only the half-precision (fp16) kernel `tanh_activation_kernel_half`, but the fixed input specification requires `dtype=torch.float32`. The AT_DISPATCH_FLOATING_TYPES_AND_HALF macro routes float32 inputs to `tanh_activation_kernel_vectorized`, completely bypassing the mutated kernel. No value-level change within float32 tensors can trigger the mutated code path. This explains why all 112 rounds of differential testing passed bitwise — the mutation is in dead code relative to the fixed input dtype.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable under fixed-shape contract. Would require changing input dtype from torch.float32 to torch.float16 to reach the mutated half-precision kernel, but dtype changes are not permitted.
rounds.recommendations: Mutation testing frameworks should consider dtype as part of the fixed configuration when determining mutant reachability. Type-dispatched kernels create implicit code paths that may be unreachable under specific dtype constraints. Test suites for CUDA kernels with multiple type specializations should include tests for each supported dtype to ensure all code paths are exercised.
